content: Croflemer has the potential to increase the levels of various medications by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which is involved in their metabolism. This effect is primarily localized to the gastrointestinal tract due to minimal systemic absorption of crofelemer. As a result, systemic inhibition of CYP3A4 is unlikely. However, close monitoring is recommended when crofelemer is co-administered with drugs metabolized by CYP3A4, as their plasma concentrations may increase, potentially leading to enhanced effects or adverse reactions. Specific examples include: 1. Amiodarone: Crofelemer may increase amiodarone levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Apixaban: Crofelemer may elevate apixaban levels. Monitor closely. 3. Aprepitant: Crofelemer may raise aprepitant levels. Monitor closely. 4. Aripiprazole: Crofelemer may increase aripiprazole levels. Monitor closely. 5. Armodafinil: Crofelemer may elevate armodafinil levels. Monitor closely. 6. Atazanavir: Crofelemer may increase atazanavir levels. Monitor closely. 7. Atogepant: Crofelemer may enhance the effect of atogepant. Monitor closely. 8. Atorvastatin: Crofelemer may raise atorvastatin levels. Monitor closely. 9. Avapritinib: Crofelemer may increase avapritinib levels. Monitor closely. 10. Axitinib: Crofelemer may elevate axitinib levels. Monitor closely. 11.
